spec.claim_summary: Enter when 5-period EMA crosses 50-period EMA and 5-period RSI crosses the 50 line on candle close.
assumptions: EMA cross compiled as 5-period EMA crosses_above 50-period EMA on bar close; claimant said only 'crosses' without direction.
RSI compiled as 5-period RSI crosses_above 50; claimant said only 'cross the 50 line' without direction.
Timeframe chosen as 1d because page chart is 1d and claimant mentions daily use; 4h use also mentioned but only one timeframe can be tested.
NOT EXPRESSIBLE: multi-timeframe (daily and 4h) use left out; tested on single timeframe.

NOT EXPRESSIBLE: strategy implies both bullish and bearish crosses (5EMA crossing 50EMA with RSI crossing 50 line for trend) but schema allows only a single direction, so only the long/bullish side is tested and the short/bearish side is omitted.
Exit not stated so opposite cross (5EMA crosses_below 50EMA) used as most common reading for this setup.

evidence.quote: I set my RSI to 5 also
on USD/CAD, EUR/USD, GBP/USD, and also EUR/JPY
I started using it on the daily and 4 hour charts
5EMA and also use a 50EMA ( for trend basically )

audit_majors: direction: Claim says '5ema crosses your 50ema' for trend with RSI crossing 50, implying both bullish and bearish signals; spec tests only long/crosses_above and omits short side. Marking it NOT EXPRESSIBLE does not fix the change to what is tested.
timeframe: Claimant explicitly uses 'daily and 4 hour charts'; spec tests only 1d and drops 4h signals. Marking multi-timeframe NOT EXPRESSIBLE still omits part of the claimed rule.
exit[0]: Claimant states no exit; spec invents exit as 5EMA crosses_below 50EMA. Invented exit determines holding period and verdict.
